overview: SUNeVision operates Hong Kong's largest carrier-neutral, cloud-neutral and cable-neutral data-centre ecosystem under the iAdvantage brand, with roughly 2.3 million sq ft of operating gross floor area and 105MW of installed IT capacity across sites including MEGA-i (Asia's top-five connectivity hub), MEGA Two, MEGA Plus, MEGA Gateway, MEGA Fanling and the flagship MEGA IDC hyperscale campus in Tseung Kwan O. The company also runs small ELV/IT-systems installation (Super e-Technology) and broadband (Super e-Network) businesses. It is majority-owned (~73-85% depending on source) by Sun Hung Kai Properties (SHKP), Hong Kong's largest property developer, which provides balance-sheet support including shareholder loans.

business_model.summary: Revenue is overwhelmingly recurring colocation/data-centre rental and power income (data centre and IT facilities), supplemented by connectivity/cross-connect fees at its MEGA-i interconnection hub, plus a small transactional ELV/IT-systems installation and broadband business. Long-term leases to hyperscale cloud, telco and enterprise tenants, plus a growing AI-inference customer base, give high revenue visibility; EBITDA margins have expanded from ~58% (FY2017) to ~74% (FY2026) as the portfolio has scaled and matured.
business_model.customer_type: B2B/wholesale and retail colocation — international and Chinese hyperscale cloud providers, AI companies, telcos, banks and enterprises
business_model.geographic_mix: 100% Hong Kong-based assets and revenue; customers are global/regional (Chinese and international hyperscalers) using Hong Kong as a connectivity gateway between mainland China and international markets

competitive_position.market_position: Largest and highest-revenue-share operator in Hong Kong's data-centre/colocation market (one third-party estimate puts iAdvantage's colocation revenue share at ~24%, the highest of any operator); majority owner of most of its own facilities versus asset-light/leased peers

moat_factors.description: MEGA-i hosts ~15,000 cross-connects and ranks among the top-5 most connected data centres globally; carrier-, cloud- and cable-neutral positioning plus 2 of Hong Kong's cable landing stations (HKIS-1, HKIS-2) create a dense interconnection ecosystem that attracts more carriers/clouds, which attracts more tenants

Majority ownership (not leasing) of its data centres, plus land tenure specifically zoned for data-centre use at MEGA IDC free of the subletting restrictions that bind HKSTP InnoPark operators; secured power capacity in a market where power is now the binding constraint on new supply

Hyperscale and enterprise tenants face high migration costs once racks, cross-connects and network routing are embedded; management cites multi-year renewal cycles with strong rental reversion on renewal
SHKP shareholder loans (HK$5bn outstanding) and balance-sheet support reduce financing risk and cost of capital versus independent operators
Hong Kong's limited land supply, lengthy power-upgrade lead times, and HKSTP InnoPark leasing disputes among smaller rivals constrain new competitive supply

weaknesses: 100% single-market (Hong Kong) concentration — no geographic diversification to de-risk local power, land or political constraints
Capital intensity: large, lumpy, multi-year capex cycles (e.g. MEGA IDC phases) with execution and leasing-up risk
High and rising absolute debt load (~HK$16bn total debt in FY2026, up from ~HK$1bn in FY2017) funding the buildout
Dependent on a concentrated set of large hyperscale/cloud tenants for a meaningful share of revenue
Subject to litigation/regulatory friction (HKSTP InnoPark enforcement dispute, HKCOLO defamation counter-suit) that creates reputational and legal cost overhang

growth_drivers: AI inference demand: management sees Hong Kong emerging as a critical regional hub for low-latency AI inference workloads (distinct from remote AI training), driving a new, structural wave of hyperscale and enterprise demand

MEGA IDC build-out: Phase One (~500,000 sq ft, 50MW) already seeing a major customer commitment lifting occupancy toward 70%+, with Phases 2 and 3 (~700,000 sq ft) being fast-tracked as a single integrated phase targeted for 2028, taking total GFA to ~3 million sq ft and power capacity from 150MW to 280MW+

Rental reversion and power upgrades on the existing (largely full) portfolio — retrofitting incumbent clients with higher power density/liquid cooling at MEGA-i and MEGA Plus, and revitalisation projects at MEGA Two that have materially increased yield per sq ft
Growing Chinese hyperscaler demand for Hong Kong capacity as a bridge to global markets and to support cross-border AI/cloud expansion
Subsea cable and connectivity ecosystem expansion (new landings such as ADC and SJC2) reinforcing MEGA-i's role as a regional traffic aggregation point
Disciplined, just-in-time capital deployment (4-6 month delivery capability) that lets the company convert demand into capex without getting ahead of committed revenue
Potential further M&A/greenfield opportunities leveraging SHKP's balance sheet and land bank

business.description: A relatively small number of large hyperscale and cloud customers account for a meaningful share of recurring revenue; loss or renegotiation of a major tenant could affect occupancy and pricing

business.risk: Execution risk on MEGA IDC buildout
business.description: Accelerating Phase 2/3 into a single integrated development by 2028 raises construction, leasing and timing risk versus the original staggered plan
Management itself flags that 'new supply from our peers is expected over the medium term,' which could erode pricing power if demand growth slows

Ongoing enforcement proceedings against a rival (HKCOLO.NET) for alleged lease breaches at the InnoPark, and a defamation counter-suit against SUNeVision, create legal cost and reputational overhang, though the company is not a direct litigant in the enforcement action

financial.description: Total debt has grown from ~HK$1bn (FY2017) to ~HK$16bn (FY2026) funding the data-centre buildout; net bank borrowings plus HK$5bn of SHKP shareholder loans mean leverage (45% gearing including shareholder loans on a fair-value basis) will need continued profitable growth or refinancing support

All borrowings are on a floating-rate basis — a benefit during the recent rate-cutting cycle but a risk if rates rise again; finance costs have already swung materially (down 25% YoY in H1 FY2026 on lower rates, having been a major drag in FY2023-24)
Large committed/discretionary capex for MEGA IDC Phase 2/3 will require continued access to bank facilities, SHKP support, and/or capital markets

regulatory.description: SUNeVision has pushed for stricter enforcement against rivals it alleges are subletting InnoPark capacity in breach of lease terms; slow or inconsistent enforcement by the statutory body is a competitive-fairness risk the company has publicly flagged

Future data-centre capacity growth in Hong Kong is explicitly gated by CLP/HEC grid capacity and government land policy; favorable or unfavorable shifts in policy materially affect the addressable growth opportunity
Evolving data localization, cross-border data flow and sustainability-linked financing/reporting requirements could add compliance costs

macro.description: 100% of assets/revenue is tied to a single city-state economy and its competitiveness as a connectivity gateway versus Singapore and other regional hubs; management itself warns Hong Kong's subsea-cable count has fallen behind Singapore's (12 vs 21 as of the report) since 2019
US-China tech tensions could affect hyperscaler capex plans, cross-border data flows, or specific customers' ability/willingness to expand in Hong Kong
A renewed rate-hiking cycle would directly raise finance costs given the floating-rate debt structure and reverse a recent earnings tailwind
Current demand is explicitly driven by a global AI buildout; a slowdown in AI infrastructure spending by hyperscalers would reduce the pipeline of large-scale deployments SUNeVision is counting on

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Hong Kong data-centre/colocation market estimated at roughly US$4-4.9bn (2025-26), growing toward US$21bn+ by the mid-2030s per third-party forecasts, driven by AI inference, cloud and hyperscale demand; global data-centre capacity demand is projected to rise sharply (McKinsey: ~82GW in 2025 to ~219GW by 2030, with AI driving most incremental growth)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate — underlying demand is structural (cloud/AI adoption) and revenue is largely recurring under multi-year leases, but capex and new-supply decisions are cyclical and tied to the broader AI capex cycle
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-high — all borrowings are floating rate; recent rate cuts have been a meaningful earnings tailwind (finance costs down 25% YoY in H1 FY2026), implying a renewed hiking cycle would be a material headwind
key_input_costs: Construction and fit-out costs for new data-centre phases
Cooling/liquid-cooling technology for high-density AI racks

recent_developments.event: FY2026 annual results (year ended 30 June 2026): revenue +6% YoY to HK$3,117m, recurring data-centre/IT revenue +8% to HK$2,856m, EBITDA +8% to HK$2,300m (margin expanded from 72% to 74%), net profit +17% to HK$1,146m; final dividend of HK14.00 cents declared, payable 24 November 2026

Management disclosed a major hyperscale customer commitment at MEGA IDC Phase One lifting occupancy from ~30% toward ~70%, two renewals with largest customers at strong positive rental reversion, and a decision to fast-track MEGA IDC Phase 2/3 as a single combined phase (~700,000 sq ft) targeted for completion in 2028 given pre-commitment demand

Chairman's commentary flagged a notable pickup in demand over H2 FY2026 from both Chinese and international hyperscalers for AI-driven deployments, alongside concern that Hong Kong's subsea-cable connectivity has fallen behind Singapore's (12 cables vs 21 as of the report, versus near-parity in 2019), urging more proactive government policy on cable landings

H1 FY2026 interim results (six months to 31 Dec 2025): revenue +3% YoY to HK$1,508m, EBITDA +4% to HK$1,096m (margin 73%), net profit +10% to HK$531m, helped by lower floating-rate finance costs; entered a six-year renewable-energy-certificate agreement with CLP Power
Board changes effective 28 November 2025: Helen Lo appointed Executive Director; Kenny Lam appointed Independent Non-Executive Director

Continued public dispute with Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation (HKSTP) over enforcement against InnoPark data-centre operators (notably HKCOLO.NET) for alleged lease/subletting breaches; HKCOLO has filed a defamation counter-suit against SUNeVision, which the company says it will defend robustly

Analyst sentiment mixed-to-positive: consensus remains 'Buy'/'Strong Buy' with price targets clustered roughly HK$7.70-10.00 (Goldman Sachs cut its target from HK$10.9 to HK$10, then reportedly to HK$7.70, while maintaining Buy); the stock has nonetheless been volatile, with a 52-week range of roughly HK$4.24-HK$8.30 and at least one sharp single-week decline reported (~18%), alongside reports of analysts trimming 2026 revenue/EPS estimates

guidance.as_of: FY2026 Annual Results / H1 FY2026 Interim Report

items.target: ~700,000 sq ft additional GFA, lifting total power capacity from 150MW to over 280MW
items.notes: Originally planned as staggered Phase 2a/2b; management is now building out the entirety of Phase Two in one go due to strong pre-commitment demand

items.target: Occupancy to increase from ~30% to over 70%
items.period: Upon full implementation of a signed major customer commitment (FY2027 timeframe)
items.notes: Negotiations ongoing with two further hyperscale customers for the remaining two floors of Phase One

items.target: On-demand/agile capex, 4-6 month delivery capability from order confirmation
items.notes: No explicit HK$ capex guidance figure disclosed; management emphasizes capital deployment strictly aligned with committed customer demand rather than speculative build

items.target: Adjusted gearing ratio (excl. shareholder loans) of ~26% at FY2026 year-end on a fair-value basis (32% as of Dec 2025 H1)
items.notes: Management states ample liquidity/financial headroom to fund medium-term growth plans without specifying a target ceiling

items.target: Final dividend of HK14.00 cents per share for FY2026
items.notes: Consistent with 17% net profit growth in FY2026

guidance.management_commentary: Chairman Kwok Ping-luen reiterated confidence that the current AI-driven demand wave for Hong Kong data-centre capacity is 'durable and structural,' but stressed the Group will not chase occupancy or growth at any cost, prioritising premium, long-life-cycle tenants and rents that reflect the scarcity value of its assets. Management highlighted power availability and secured land tenure as the key competitive differentiator as power becomes the binding constraint on new supply across the market, and flagged advanced negotiations on several large-scale customer mandates that could underpin growth for years, while cautioning that commercial discipline (not speed) will govern which deals are signed.

bull_case: Structural, multi-year AI-inference demand wave for Hong Kong data-centre capacity, with SUNeVision already serving substantially all major US and Chinese cloud/AI companies and holding the scarcest, highest-specification capacity in a supply-constrained market

Dominant local market position (largest colocation revenue share, top-tier connectivity hub MEGA-i) combined with secured land/power gives a structural moat that is difficult for new entrants to replicate given Hong Kong's power and land constraints

Strong recent execution: FY2026 net profit +17%, EBITDA margin expanded to 74%, MEGA IDC Phase One occupancy inflecting sharply higher on a single major customer win, with Phase 2/3 being accelerated on pre-commitment demand

Falling interest-rate environment has been a direct earnings tailwind (finance costs -25% YoY in H1 FY2026) given 100% floating-rate debt, and SHKP parent backing (shareholder loans, balance-sheet support) reduces financing risk

Analyst consensus skews bullish (Buy/Strong Buy, targets ~HK$7.70-10) implying significant potential upside from recent depressed trading levels (stock has traded as low as ~HK$4.24 over the past year versus an ~8.30 high)
bear_case: 100% single-market (Hong Kong) concentration leaves the business fully exposed to local power-grid constraints, land policy, political/geopolitical risk, and competitiveness versus rising regional hubs like Singapore, which management itself says has outpaced Hong Kong on subsea-cable connectivity

Elevated and rising leverage (total debt ~HK$16bn, up from ~HK$1bn a decade ago) funding an aggressive, lumpy capex programme (MEGA IDC Phase 2/3 in one combined, accelerated build) creates execution and refinancing risk if AI capex demand or interest rates turn

Demand, while currently strong, is explicitly tied to the global AI infrastructure capex cycle; any slowdown or pause in hyperscaler/AI spending would directly hit the pipeline of 'large-scale customer mandates' management is counting on

New competitive supply is expected from peers over the medium term per management's own commentary, and ongoing litigation/regulatory friction around HKSTP InnoPark enforcement (including a rival's defamation suit against the company) adds legal and reputational overhang

Stock has shown material volatility and analysts have reportedly trimmed 2026 revenue/EPS estimates even as price targets stayed roughly flat, suggesting execution or demand-timing risk is already being discounted by at least part of the sell-side
